label: prf:fai-projector-coadjoint-orbit
title: Proof of the projector / coadjoint-orbit identification
html:
Proof. (1) Embedding via rank-1 projectors. Let \rho \colon V \to V be a rank-1 projector in \mathbf{C}: an endomorphism satisfying \rho^2 = \rho and \mathrm{tr}(\rho) = \mathrm{id}_{\mathbf{1}} (categorical trace via evaluation and coevaluation). Since V has categorical dimension 2, define the traceless component

  \sigma(\rho) = \rho - \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{id}_V
   \in  \mathrm{Ad}(A).

This is well-defined because \mathrm{tr}(\sigma(\rho)) = 1 - \tfrac{1}{2} \cdot 2 = 0. The set of such projectors is precisely \mathbb{P}(V) = G/T, the quotient by the maximal torus.

(2) The involution. Under the positive-definite involutive structure \dagger (involutive structure), every rank-1 projector satisfies \rho^{\dagger} = \rho (self-adjointness). Computing the square of the traceless component:

  \sigma(\rho)^2
  = \bigl(\rho - \tfrac{1}{2}\mathrm{id}_V\bigr)^2
  = \rho^2 - \rho + \tfrac{1}{4}\mathrm{id}_V
  = \tfrac{1}{4}\mathrm{id}_V.

Thus 2\sigma(\rho) is an involution in \mathrm{End}(V): it squares to the identity. Geometrically, \sigma identifies \mathbb{P}(V) with a coadjoint orbit in \mathrm{Ad}(A). The orbit is closed by rigidity of \mathbf{C} and determines a sub-object of \mathrm{Ad}(A) isomorphic to \mathbb{P}(V). Conversely, given this sub-object, the stabiliser of any point is T, so \mathbb{P}(V) \cong G/T as G-spaces. \square
